relationships.subject: dorsal horn PVINs
relationships.evidence_quote: Parvalbumin expressing interneurons (PVINs) within the dorsal horn (DH) of the spinal cord play an important role in allodynia whereby their inhibitory connections prevent innocuous touch information from exciting nociceptive pathways.

key_findings: Dorsal horn PVINs in aged mice show increased intrinsic excitability (shift from initial bursting to tonic firing) with unchanged overall excitatory and inhibitory drive.
PVIN inhibitory output onto unidentified dorsal horn neurons strengthens with age and shifts toward GABAergic transmission.
